_about: One entry per app version. The pre-push gate (tools/release_docs_gate.py) refuses to push a version without one. Each field says 'updated: what' or 'n/a: why'. guide = the in-app user guide (and menucaptain-help.md via export_help.js); promo = the living promo inventory (CG Apps\MenuCaptain\MenuCaptain Promo\living-promo-template.html); email_notes = next issue's notes (MenuCaptain Updates\next-issue-notes.md); welcome = welcome.html, the public promo page; handoff = HANDOFF.md section + BRIEFING.md rows + a MenuCaptain Log entry. Started 2026-10-16 after Chris asked, again, that every document stay current.

1.587.0.what: Fixes and Chris's past asks (chosen by card 2026-11-08). (1) In the iPhone app, links handed to other people (group order, group vote, shared visit, shared place lists) read capacitor://localhost and did nothing (Chris found it on a group order); they now always use https://menucaptain.com/ (shareBase). (2) Group order: 'Who is this?' on an Also ordered row relabels that order to a waiting name on your list and remembers the phone (Chris: Gracie ordered as 'G'); a lone initial now raises the same-person question, and a merge keeps the fuller name. (3) The free-limit message in the iPhone app says plainly what is used up and that everything else keeps working (no 'for now': the allowance is one-time). (4) A website typed for a place that had none is kept on the place. (5) 'Open now' on Find a place's and the at-restaurant finder's Google results. (6) Wording: 'friends' not 'connections', 'Read the check' without a bracketed count, group-order share text no longer assumes the host is at the place, the guide's sharing example uses the demo name.

1.596.3.what: For everyone: the app keeps clear of the strips a phone reserves down its sides, on any phone. On the iPhone Duo's outer screen the clock sits in a column down the right edge (the phone reports it as about 84 points), and the top bar's chat and Settings buttons ran under it (Chris, 2026-11-25, with a screenshot). The app used to read only the top and bottom of the phone's safe area; it now reads the sides too. An ordinary iPhone held upright reports nothing on its sides, so nothing moves there. Also: text shows at the app's own sizes. iPhones were enlarging some blocks of text on their own, unevenly (on Chris's Duo the group order screen showed Molly's name bigger than Sam's), so the app now turns that off (-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%).
